drawdown.name: Drawdown
drawdown.measures: How far the S&P 500 is below its high of the past year.
drawdown.why: There is no bottom to call until the market has fallen at least 10%. Below that line, the five checks start to count.

vix.name: VIX above 30
vix.measures: The volatility traders expect over the next 30 days, priced from S&P 500 options. Above 30 signals fear.
vix.why: Bottoms tend to form when fear peaks and sellers run out.

fed.name: Fed not signaling hikes
fed.measures: The 2-year Treasury yield minus the Fed's upper target rate. Above zero means traders expect the Fed to raise rates.
fed.why: Selloffs recover more easily when the Fed is not tightening into them.

margin.name: Margin debt deleveraging
margin.measures: Two readings of how much borrowed money is in stocks. FINRA's monthly total of what investors owe their brokers, which arrives about three weeks after each month ends. And a weekly CFTC count of S&P 500 futures held by hedge funds and other leveraged traders, which is about three days old.
margin.why: A sharp drop in either means forced selling has mostly happened, and fewer leveraged holders are left to sell. For now only FINRA decides this check. The weekly futures reading is shown for reference while its rule is tuned, because futures holdings also rise and fall with each quarterly contract expiry.

sector.name: A clear leading sector
sector.measures: The sector fund beating the S&P 500 by the most over the last 20 trading days.
sector.why: New uptrends usually have a leader that money moves into early.

nvda.name: NVIDIA beats earnings
nvda.measures: Whether NVIDIA's latest earnings per share beat Wall Street's estimate.
nvda.why: NVIDIA is the bellwether of the AI trade. A beat during a selloff shows the core story still holds.
